topicName: Introduction to ETL vs ELT Architecture
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to ETL vs ELT Architecture"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data integration is the backbone of modern analytics and business intelligence. As organizations collect massive volumes of data from diverse sources, choosing the right data pipeline architecture becomes critical. The two primary paradigms for data integration are ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) and ELT (Extract, Load, Transform)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding ETL (Extract, Transform, Load)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"ETL is the traditional approach to data integration. In this architecture, data is extracted from source systems, transformed into a clean, structured format in a staging area (often using a dedicated ETL server), and finally loaded into the target data warehouse."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Extract: Gathering raw data from operational databases, CRM systems, or API endpoints."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Transform: Cleaning, filtering, masking, and aggregating data on a separate processing server before storage."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Load: Writing the finalized, structured data into the destination data warehouse."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding ELT (Extract, Load, Transform)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"ELT is a modern evolution made possible by the rise of cloud data warehouses like Snowflake, Google BigQuery, and Amazon Redshift. In ELT, data is extracted from the source and immediately loaded into the target data warehouse in its raw format. The transformation phase occurs inside the data warehouse itself utilizing its massive parallel processing (MPP) power."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Extract: Collecting raw data from source systems."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Load: Directly dumping raw, unstructured, or semi-structured data into the cloud data warehouse."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Transform: Executing SQL queries or using tools like dbt (data build tool) to transform data directly inside the warehouse storage layer."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Differences in Code Implementation"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"The fundamental operational difference can be illustrated by where the data processing logic executes. In ELT, SQL is typically used to transform raw JSON or tabular data directly within the target database."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE processed_sales AS SELECT order_id, customer_id, CAST(order_date AS DATE) AS sale_date, revenue * exchange_rate AS revenue_usd FROM raw_sales_data WHERE status = 'COMPLETED';"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Choosing Between ETL and ELT"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use ETL when dealing with strict compliance or on-premise legacy systems where sensitive data must be scrubbed before touching the central repository."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use ELT when utilizing scalable cloud data warehouses, working with big data or semi-structured data formats (JSON, XML), and requiring faster pipeline setup times."}]
